Happymodel's product post prints the block: Output power: 25~200mw switchable, Frequency: 40CH, Input voltage: 4.8v~5.5v, Current consumption: 250mA~510mA(type), Antenna: RG178 antenna U.FL interface, Frequency: 5.8GHz 5bands 40 channels, With Raceband, Smartaudio ready, Weight: 3g without antenna, plus the recorder rows: Video Output Size VGA (640x480), Video Output format NTSC, Record video size 1280x720 @25FPS, TF Card support Max.32G, Compress Format AVI. power_levels_mw is the manual's own instruction - "set vtx_power=1" is 25mw, "=2" 100mw, "=3" 200mw - and that manual prints the same 5-band 40-channel table (Band1 5865-5725, Band5 5658-5917 MHz). A transmitter that records to its own TF card on the VTX board rather than in the goggles; recording starts automatically at power-on and the manual warns there is no auto-save at power-off.

Happymodel's own post for the OVX300 and OVX303 prints the block: Model: OVX300, Frequency: 5.8G 40CH, Transmitting Power: 0/RCE/25mw/100mw/300mw, Power supply: DC 5V, Current (5v): <650ma (300mw), Weight: 0.9gram without antenna, Standard size: 14*15*3mm. It confirms the two figures this page already carried off the retail listing (300 mW, 0.9 g) and adds the channel count, the input voltage and the power steps. 14*15*3mm is the board, not a pattern: the OVX300 states no mounting holes at all - that is the OVX303's half of the same post - so mount_mm stays empty. power_levels_mw keeps the steps stated in milliwatts; the list also carries a step labelled 'RCE' between 0 and 25 whose power is never given a figure. The Betaflight vtxtable pasted under the blocks is not a source for this column: its powerlabels read '0 RCE 25 100 400' on a page whose two spec blocks both say 300, so it is the OVX306's table.

Corrected against Happymodel's own post, whose OVX303 block reads: Model: OVX303, Frequency: 5.8G 40CH, Transmitting Power: 0/RCE/25mw/100mw/300mw, Power supply: DC 5V, Current (5v): <650ma (300mw), Weight: 1.5gram without antenna, Center distance of mounting holes: 16mmx16mm / 20mmx20mm / 25.5mmx25.5mm. The 0.9 g this page used to show came from RaceDayQuads' listing, which also prints 'Dimensions: 15x14mm' - both are the *OVX300's* figures from the same Happymodel post ('Weight: 0.9gram without antenna', 'Standard size: 14*15*3mm'), so the listing is partly its sibling's listing. mount_mm now keeps all three patterns the manufacturer states, as the stacks do; the listing's 'Stack Size: 16x16mm, 20x20mm, 25x25mm' differs in its last entry and 25.5x25.5 is the pattern frames are sold for. power_levels_mw keeps the steps stated in milliwatts; the list also carries an 'RCE' step with no figure.

Happymodel's own product post prints the labelled block: Model: OVX306, Frequency: 5.8G 48CH, Transmitting Power: 0/RCE/25mw/100mw/400mw, Power supply: DC 5V, Current (5v): <650ma (400mw), Weight: 1.5gram without antenna, Center distance of mounting holes: 25.5mmx25.5mm. power_levels_mw keeps only the steps the page states in milliwatts - the list also carries a step labelled 'RCE' between 0 and 25 whose power is never given a figure. frequency_range keeps the 5.8 GHz class label this column uses for the band; the two Betaflight vtxtables pasted on the same page (SmartAudio and Tramp) run from 5333 MHz (LOWRACE L1) to 5917 MHz (Raceband R8). No antenna connector is recorded: the page says only that the module is 'the same size as whoop_vtx and whoop_vtx_hp, and the interface are also exactly the same', which is a compatibility statement about two other boards and not this one's own spec. Sold as the replacement for the discontinued whoop_VTX and whoop_VTX_hp, and the transmitter the Cine8 kit has shipped with since 25 Feb 2022. Runs the open-source OpenVTx firmware, so both SmartAudio and Tramp are supported and detected automatically.

Happymodel's product post prints the block: Output power: 25~200mw switchable, Frequency: 40CH, Input voltage: 3.3V 5.5V, Current consumption: 300mA(type), Antenna: RG178 antenna U.FL interface, Frequency: 5.8GHz 5bands 40 channels, With Raceband, Smartaudio ready, Weight: 2g without antenna. input_voltage is that line read as the range it prints without a separator. power_levels_mw is off the one-page manual, which labels the board's three power test points 25MW, 100MW and 200MW and prints the 5-band 40-channel table (Band1 5865-5725, Band5/Raceband 5658-5917 MHz). The same manual carries a warning worth repeating: 'In the Smartaudio control menu, the vtx power is actually 200mw when it shows 500mw and it's actually 100mw when it shows 200mw' - this radio's own on-screen menu prints power steps it does not have, so an OSD photograph is not a source for this column. Discontinued; Happymodel names the OVX306 as the replacement.

Happymodel's product post prints the block: Brand name: happymodel, Item name: whoop_VTX_hp, Output power: 25~400mw switchable, Frequency: 40CH, Input voltage: 5V, Current consumption: 400mA(type), Antenna: directional linear U.FL interface, Frequency: 5.8GHz 5bands 40 channels, With Raceband, Smartaudio ready, Weight: 2.8g with antenna. weight_g is deliberately empty: the only weight the page states includes the antenna, and every other weight in this column is the module without one. The 'Package included' line on the same page reads '1x happymodel whoop_VTX_hp 5.8G 40CH 25mW~200mW Switchable VTX' - the non-HP board's figure copied into the HP's packing list; the post title, the spec block and the discontinuation notice all say 25~400 mW, so the packing list is the error. power_levels_mw is empty because the page states a range and no steps. Discontinued, with the OVX306 named as the replacement; this is the transmitter the Cine8 kit shipped with before 25 Feb 2022.

HDZero's own product page prints the labelled block: Model HDZero Eco VTX, SKU HDZ3160, Frequency 5.8G, Resolution Default 1280*720@60fps, RF power 25mw/200mw, RF Connector U.FL, Interface Composite HD, Size 32.4x32.5mm (29x29mm inner), Weight 4.5grames/4mm Thickness (w/o shielding), Power 1000mA@5V, power input 1S-3S, Mounting 25.5x25.2 M2 soft mounting. The one VTX in the HDZero line that takes composite HD video over a single wire instead of a MIPI cable, which is why it pairs with the LUX/Eco camera and not with the MIPI cameras the rest of the system uses. mount_mm and input_voltage are the HDZero VTX User Manual v1.1 figures (p2 product table: 25.5x25.5, M2 (Soft), 4.5grams, 4V-12V, 5~6W, RF power output 25mW/200mW), because three manufacturer statements of the mounting pattern disagree in the last digit - 25.5x25.2 on the product page, '25 x 25 M2 Soft Mounting' on the Eco Bundle page and 25.5x25.5 in the manual - and 25.5x25.5 is the only one of the three that is a pattern frames are sold for. The manual's own Dimension row for this model (29x30) is not used: it repeats the Freestyle V2's figure and contradicts the product page's 32.4x32.5mm. channels is the manual's 'All VTXes support R1-R8, E1, F1, F2 and F4 channels' (p8), twelve; eight more (L1-L8) appear only after the low-band unlock firmware is flashed.

Manufacturer source 2026-09-23, and it names the part: this is the HDZero Freestyle V1, which the HDZero VTX User Manual v1.1 lists under 'Discontinued Video Transmitters' (p22) at 40x40 mm body, 30x30 M3 (Soft) mounting, 28 grams, 2S-6S power input, 6~15W, RF power output '25mW,200mW (500mW, 1W if with HAM license)', Secured U.FL, RHCP antenna included. The 28 g and the 30x30 pattern this page already published are that row exactly, which is how the retail title's 'Freestyle 30x30' is pinned to a model name. The manual adds (p28) that the first batch supports 2S-4S and ships with a 2S-6S BEC, the second batch and later 2S-6S with no BEC, and that the heat sink is part of the design. HDZero's shop no longer lists it, so there is no product page to cite - the manual is the whole manufacturer record.

items.model: Freestyle V2 20x20 25-1000mW Digital HD Kit - U.FL
items.note: Second source 2026-09-23: this kit is the Freestyle V2 VTX plus a Nano 90 V2 camera (19x19 mount) and an RHCP antenna, and HDZero's kit page reprints the transmitter's block verbatim - 22.3 g, 29x30x14mm, 5.725-5.850GHz, Transmitter Power 25mW,200mW, 20x20mm M2 holes, Secured U.FL, Input Power 7-25V, 6-15W - with the same sentence that the VTX is capable of 1W at R1 once unlocked with a licence. weight_g stays empty on purpose: 22.3 g is the transmitter and this SKU is a box with a camera and an antenna in it, and no source weighs the box.

Second source 2026-09-23: HDZero's own product page prints the labelled block - Manufacturer Divimath, Inc, Model HDZero Freestyle V2 VTX, Weight 22.3 g, Dimensions 29x30x14mm, Operating Frequency 5.725-5.850GHz, Transmitter Power 25mW,200mW, Mounting Pattern 20x20mm M2 holes, Antenna Interface Secured U.FL, Video In Secured MIPI, Input Power 7-25V, Power Consumption 6-15W - and the 1 W this page publishes is the same manufacturer's, stated twice outside that block: 'The VTX is capable of maximum 1W RF output at R1 channel if unlocked with license or approval from the local authorities' on the product page, and in the HDZero VTX User Manual v1.1 (linked from hd-zero.com/document), p2 'HDZero VTX Products' table as '25mW, 200mW (500mW, 1W with HAM license unlock)', with an Unlock RF Power Limit procedure on p18 citing FCC 47 CFR 97.215(c). So max_power_mw is the radio and power_levels_mw records that it ships limited to 200 mW; output also decreases as the channel frequency rises above R1. This is the TBS Unify Pro32 DP case from the other direction - there a retail title printed a locked-down subset as the whole radio, here the manufacturer's own spec block does.

Manufacturer source 2026-09-23: the HDZero VTX User Manual v1.1 lists the Race V2 under 'Discontinued Video Transmitters' (p22) at 34x34 mm body, 20x20 M4 (Soft) mounting, 6 grams, 7V-17V (2S-4S) power input, 5~6W, RF power output 25mW,200mW, Secured U.FL, no antenna included, and its own page (p26) labels the board '20x20 M4 mounting holes' with a 'Rubber Grommet (M4 to M3)' - the same hole-versus-screw pair as the Race V3. weight_g stays at the retailer's 5.9 g rather than moving to the manual's 6 grams: the manual's table rounds every weight in it to a whole gram (7, 6, 28) and 5.9 is the same figure at the resolution the column holds. HDZero's shop no longer lists this model.

Second source 2026-09-23: HDZero's own product page prints the labelled block the retail listing paraphrases - Model HDZero Race V3, SKU HDZ3143, Frequency 5.725-5.850GHz, Resolution Default 540p90/720p60/1080p30, RF power 25mw/200mw, RF Connector Secured U.FL, Interface 4 lane MIPI CSI YUV422, Size 32mm x 28mm x 5mm, Weight 5.5g, Harness length 40mm, power input 4V-12V, Mounting 20mm x 20mm M4 with rubber grommets. It confirms the 200 mW, the 5.5 g and the 5.725-5.850 GHz already published and adds the two power steps and the input range. mount_mm gains the screw size: the holes are M4 and the included 'Rubber Grommet (M4 to M3)' reduces them to M3 screws, which is why the HDZero VTX User Manual v1.1 (linked from hd-zero.com/document), p2 'HDZero VTX Products' table prints the same pattern as '20x20 M3 (Soft)' - the table names the screw that goes through the grommet, the product page names the hole. channels is the manual's 'All VTXes support R1-R8, E1, F1, F2 and F4 channels' (p8); L1-L8 exist only after the low-band unlock firmware.

Manufacturer source 2026-09-23, and it survives only on its successor's page: HDZero has discontinued the Whoop Lite, so there is no product page for it, but the Whoop V2's page prints a 'Whoop Lite VTX Comparison' column that states its figures - Standard U.FL (no retention bar), Size 32.5x32.5 mm (29x29 inner), Weight 4.9 g (4.6 g w/o wires), Board Thickness ~1.2 mm (no shielding), recommended use 65-85 mm whoops - and the HDZero VTX User Manual v1.1 keeps its own page for it (p24): 720p60, 'capable of delivering up to 200mW on 5.8GHz', power input range 2.8V - 13V, no reverse polarity protection, M2 gummies for soft mounting, zip ties for antenna retention, and removable grounded protection cases on both sides. weight_g is the 4.9 g with the wires, the same as-shipped basis as the Whoop V2's 5.4 g. power_levels_mw is the manual's selectable pair (p8, 'selectable between 25mW, 200mW'). mount_mm keeps the retailer's 25x25mm: the manufacturer states M2 soft mounting for this model but prints no pattern for it anywhere, so there is nothing to correct it with.

Manufacturer source 2026-09-23: the radio in this bundle is the Whoop Lite, discontinued by HDZero and documented in the HDZero VTX User Manual v1.1 (p24) - 720p60, up to 200mW on 5.8GHz, power input 2.8V-13V, M2 gummies for soft mounting - and in the 'Whoop Lite VTX Comparison' column of the Whoop V2's product page. frequency_range was '5.727-5.850 GHz', a figure that appears in one retail line and nowhere else: the same retailer's page for the bare module says 5.8 GHz, every other HDZero page says 5.725-5.850 GHz, and no manufacturer source prints a 5.727 edge, so this holds the band label HDZero itself uses for the model. weight_g stays empty: 4.9 g is the transmitter and this SKU is a bundle.

HDZero states this VTX has no reverse-polarity protection circuit, which it calls the number one failure cause.

The columns hold the transmitter, so weight_g stays the 5.4 g of the module and not the bundle, which also contains the camera, a dipole antenna and a 40mm MIPI cable. channels is the manual's R1-R8, E1, F1, F2, F4 (p8).

HGLRC's own labelled block: 'Product Name: 3.3G 5W Video Transmitter, Input Voltage: DC 7-36V, Operating Frequency: 3060MHz-3500MHz, Available Channels: 64-CH, Max Output Power: 5W, Max Dimensions (LWH): 48.5mm 35mm 21.5mm, Mounting Hole Pattern: 20X20mm * M2, Output Power: "PIT/300mW /1W /3W/5W", Signal-to-Noise Ratio S/N (Fo+-3MHz): >55dBc, Antenna Port Impedance: 50 Ohms, Input Signal Format: NTSC or PAL, Operating Temperature: -10C ~ +60C, Weight: 52g'. frequency_range is the span of the page's own 8x8 frequency chart, which runs 3060 MHz (FR1 CH1) to 3500 MHz (FR8 CH8) and matches the stated operating frequency; the '3.3G' of the title is the class label. power_levels_mw follows the product page, which states the same list three times - the advantages line ('4 adjustable power levels: PIT/300mW/1W/3W/5W'), the function description ('cycle through power levels: 300mW/1W/3W/5W') and the spec block. HGLRC's own Specification graphic on the same page prints the low step as 25mW instead ('Output power: 25mW/1W/3W/5W'), and that panel is the unreliable one: its size row says 64mmX37mmX18mm against the dimension drawing in the same image, which says 48.5/35/21.5 like the text. Neither figure is version-tagged, so this is not the BetaFPV M03's two hardware revisions; it is one panel carrying a number the rest of the brand's material does not. max_power_mw is 5000 on either reading. A 3.3 GHz link needs a licence in most countries; check local rules before transmitting.

HGLRC's own labelled block: 'Input Voltage: DC 7-36V, Operating Frequency: 4900~6000MHz, Available Channels: 80-CH, Maximum Output Power: 10W, Dimensions (L*W*H): 60.5mm x 36mm x 25mm, Mounting Hole Pattern: 20 x 20mm, M2 holes, Output Power Levels: PIT / 25mW / 200mW / 5W / 10W, Signal-to-Noise Ratio S/N (Fo+-3MHz): >70dBc, Antenna Port Impedance: 50 Ohms, Input Signal Format: NTSC or PAL, Operating Temperature: -10C ~ +60C, Weight: 73.2g', and the brand's own Parameters graphic on the same page repeats every row of it. power_levels_mw drops the PIT step, which has no figure. weight_g is the module's own: the dimension drawing prints 'weight: 73.2g' beside 'Total weight: 109.4g' for the boxed set (128x81.6x36.3mm), and the labelled block's Weight row is the 73.2. This is a wideband 4.9-6.0 GHz radio whose case silkscreen, product graphic and packing list all call it '5.8G 10W VTX' while the shop title calls it '4.9-6Ghz 10W High-Power VTX'; the model name here keeps the band the spec block measures, because that is the class this catalogue files it in. Wideband 4.9-6.0 GHz output is the Ukrainian long-range class - most of the span needs a licence or is outside the amateur allocation in the EU and US, so check local rules before transmitting.

HGLRC's own labelled block, printed identically in the page text and in the brand's Product parameters graphic: 'Product name: 5.8G 2.5W VTX, Support voltage: DC 7-26V (2-6S), BEC: 5V/800mA, Antenna interface: MMCX, Cable interface: GH1.25 6P, Video format: PAL/NTSC, Standard 40 channels: A/B/E/F/R frequency group, Protocol: TBS SmartAudio, Output power: PIT/25/200/800/1600mW/2500mW, Installation hole position: 30.5*30.5*M3, Dimensions (L*W*H): 40mm x 35mm x 11.8mm, Weight: 19.6g', with a dBm equivalent per step (25mW/13.95, 200mW/23.01, 800mW/29.03, 1.6W/32.04, 2.5W/33.98 dBm). power_levels_mw drops the PIT step, which has no figure. weight_g is the module's own: the dimension drawing prints 'Weight: 19.6g' beside 'Total weight: 34.8g' for the boxed set. The shop's own URL calls this part 'zeus-vtx-2-5w' and the title omits any model name at all, while the brand's graphic, the spec block and the case label all say 5.8G 2.5W VTX and no Zeus mark appears on the board; the block's name is the one used here.

HGLRC's own labelled block, printed identically in the page text and in the brand's Parameters graphic: 'Product name: 5.8G 5.5W VTX, Support voltage: DC 7-36V (2-8S), Antenna interface: SMA, Cable interface: GH1.25 6P, Video format: PAL/NTSC, Standard 64 channels: A/B/E/F/R/O/L/X frequency group, Protocol: TBS SmartAudio, Output power: PIT/25mW/1000mW/2000mW/3000mW/5500mW, Installation hole: 20*20*M2, Dimensions (L*W*H): 80.33mm x36.06mm x 18.37mm, Weight: 68.6g', with a dBm equivalent per step (25mW/13.95, 1000mW/30.00, 2000mW/33.01, 3000mW/34.77, 5500mW/37.40 dBm) - conducted milliwatts, not an EIRP. power_levels_mw drops the PIT step, which has no figure. weight_g is the module's own: the dimension drawing prints 'weight: 68.6g' beside 'Total weight: 108.1g' for the boxed set. frequency_range keeps the 5.8 GHz class label the brand titles it with; the page's advantages line also claims 'you can directly input any frequency point within 4.9-5.8G', which is a tuning claim in prose rather than a stated band, and the O/L/X groups above and below the standard five are where that span comes from.

HGLRC's own labelled block: 'Model: 5.8G VTX PRO 1.6W, Built-in Microphone, Antenna interface: MMCX, Output power: PIT/25/400/800/1.6W, Standard 40 Frequency Point: A/B/E/F/R frequency group, VTX protocol: TBS SmartAudio, Installing Hole: 20X20.M2, Size: 25mm x 37mm x 6.5mm, Weight: 13g', with the per-step dBm list beside it (25mW/13.95dBm, 400mW/26.02dBm, 800mW/29.03dBm, 1.6W/32.04dBm) - conducted milliwatts with a dBm equivalent per step, not an EIRP. power_levels_mw drops the PIT step, which has no figure. input_voltage is deliberately EMPTY: the product page's block says 'Input voltage: DC 6-26V' and the brand's own Specification graphic on the same page says 'Support voltage: 7-36V', two manufacturer figures for one field, so neither is published (the rule the iFlight BLITZ Whoop 1.6W's mount set). Both sources agree on the 5V/500mA BEC the other line of that pair states.

Cited to HGLRC, whose own labelled block reads: 'Model: Zeus VTX 800mW, Built-in Microphone, Input voltage: DC 6-26V, Output voltage: 5V/2A, Antenna interface: MMCX, Output power: PIT/25/100/200/400/800mW, Frequency: 5.8GHz 5 bands, 40 channels, Installing Hole: 20X20/30X30mm.M3, Size: 37mm x 37mm x 5mm, Weight: 4.8g, Protocol: IRC tramp', with a current draw per step (PIT@94mA, 25mW@169mA/14dBm, 100mW@199mA/20dBm, 200mW@216mA/23dBm, 400mW@279mA/26dBm, 800mW@387mA/29dBm) - conducted milliwatts with a dBm equivalent, not an EIRP. The 800 mW, 40 channels, MMCX and 4.8 g the retail listing gave us are all confirmed. mount_mm gains the second pattern the board is named for: this is the 'Smart Mounting' Zeus, whose ears carry both a 20x20 and a 30x30 hole set (both visible in HGLRC's own board photographs), and the scrape had only the 20x20 from the retail title.

Cited to HGLRC, whose own labelled block reads: 'Model: Zeus nano VTX, CE Certified, Built-in Microphone, Input voltage: DC 5V, Antenna interface: ipex, Output power: PIT/25/100/200/350mW, Standard 40 channels. A/B/E/F/R frequency group, Installing Hole: 16X16/25.5X25.5mm.M2 / 20X20mm.M3, Size: 18.6mm x 13.6mm x 6mm, Weight: 2.4g, Protocol: IRC tramp', with a current draw per step (PIT@75mA, 25mW@180mA/16dBm, 100mW@280mA/21.5dBm, 200mW@330mA/24.5dBm, 350mW@400mA/27.5dBm). The brand's own photograph annotates the three hole sets on the board - 25.5*25.5mm M2, 20*20mm M3, 16*16mm M2 - and its scale photo shows the 2.4 g. mount_mm is corrected to those three: the retail title sells it as '16x16/20x20/25x25' and 25x25 is not a pattern HGLRC states, the Happymodel OVX303's third figure one brand over (25.5 is the pattern frames are sold for). model_set carries the same correction into the name; the slug keeps the 25x25 it was minted with, because a published URL does not move. 'ipex' is this column's U.FL.

iFlight's product page prints the labelled block: Item: BLITZ RACE 25mW VTX, Input voltage: DC 7-26V, Volts input: 2-6S, LED lamp output voltage 5V current 2A, Fixed transmitting power: 25mW(14dbm), Antenna connector: IPEX, VTX input connector: SH0.8 4P, LED connector: SH0.8 3P. power_levels_mw is deliberately empty: this radio has no selectable power, and both the block and the feature list call the figure fixed - so max_power_mw here is the only power the board has, not the top of a list. channels is the manual's own frequency table (B015949_BLITZ RACE 25mW VTX Instructions_20241030.pdf), which prints ONE band - RACE, CH1-CH8, 5658-5917 MHz - and whose LED legend says the channel is 'cycled in RACE BAND 1-8CH'; the product page states no channel count at all, and this is the only transmitter in this column locked to a single band. mount_mm is the page's own 'Double mounting holes: 30.5*30.5mm / 20*20mm'. antenna_connector is normalised to the column's U.FL spelling; iFlight writes IPEX in the block and 'iPex/UFL' in the same page's packing list ('1 x iPex/UFL to M2 SMA F Adapter Cable'), which is the same connector. weight_g is empty: neither the page nor the manual states one. The board carries an LED-strip controller (5V 2A output on an SH0.8 3P connector), which is why it also has a colour button.

iFlight's own product page prints the labelled block: Input voltage: 7V~34V, Interface: MMCX, Power levels: PIT/25mW/400mW/800mW/1600mW, Channels: 48 (including Raceband), Mounting pattern: 30.5x30.5mm/Φ3, Lightweight: 18.9g (excluding antenna), VTX telemetry: IRC Tramp. channels was 40 off the retail listing and is 48: the manual's frequency table (BLITZ 1.6W VTX Manual.pdf) is six bands of eight, A-B-E-F-R-L, and the page says 48 twice. model is iFlight's own name for the radio: the retail title 'Blitz 30x30 25-1000mW+ 5.8GHz - MMCX' prints a top step of 1000mW+ for a radio whose maker lists 1600 mW, and a 30x30 class for a board the maker measures at 30.5x30.5mm. The slug keeps the name it was minted with. max_power_mw 1600, mount_mm 30.5x30.5mm and weight_g 18.9 were already right and are now cited to the manufacturer; the manual rounds the same weight to 19g.
